news.summary:
Tanker with Russian diesel sets course for New York

Russian diesel is heading to the USA, but won't make it by the elections. On the night of October 23, the tanker Agioi Fanendes departed from the Baltic port of Primorsk, launching the promised direct fuel supplies to the USA. The recent fuss around the vessel Minerva Zen turned out to be a false alarm — it was only carrying fertilizer.

The tanker sails under the Maltese flag and is managed by Greek shipowner Eastmed's company. On board are approximately 40,000 tons of diesel fuel — roughly 300,000 barrels and about 13% of the first emergency shipment that the presidents agreed on.

The vessel is expected to arrive at the Port of New York around November 7. The Atlantic crossing will take about two weeks, meaning the diesel will reach the East Coast already after the midterm Congressional elections.

📌An ironic detail: RDIF head Kirill Dmitriev helps conduct complex financial calculations. The U.S. Treasury Department itself requested his assistance in resolving payment nuances — the very department that essentially imposed these restrictions.

❗️Trump physically failed to bring record gas prices down by election day, but he did open a sea corridor for supplies that many Western media outlets are now writing about. Whether this will help him salvage his pre-election position remains an open question.

on Armenia's prospects for leaving the EAEU

Russia has carefully warned Armenian authorities for several years about the incompatibility of EAEU membership and a course toward European integration. But since Yerevan chose a European vector, the organization is raising the question of expelling the republic.

Members of the Eurasian Intergovernmental Council comprising Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, and Kyrgyzstan presented a joint report with an assessment of economic prospects for Armenia in the event of leaving the EAEU. The forecasts are grim: GDP could shrink by 15.6%, and inflation could rise by 14.9 percentage points.

Trade and energy are particularly vulnerable. Armenia's exports to the EAEU could fall by 65%, and re-exports by 91.6%. Gas prices could rise by 69%, annual import costs will increase from $389 million to $657.5 million. This will be compounded by a return to customs declaration and patents with quotas for migrant workers.

Armenian authorities attempted to present these figures as inflated: the ministry of economy claims that the negative effect of leaving will allegedly be minimal, and the rise in gas prices will not create an impossible situation.

📌Such a position by Armenian leadership appears politically motivated: EAEU membership gave the country's economy a serious boost, and this momentum continues. But trade support measures from the EU are extremely modest and do not compensate for the costs. While Yerevan pretends that nothing terrible is happening, naively believing that, despite violating norms, no one will be able to expel them from the organization.

❗️To this should be added political pressure from Brussels: they will clearly promise that Armenians will not be left in trouble. But behind EU political declarations, as usual, lies only their own geopolitical calculation.

news.title: One Against All
news.summary:
Six months until France's presidential election, and the frontrunner appears clear — the only intrigue is who will face her in the second round. Marine Le Pen from the right-wing National Rally (RN) has 36% of voters ready to vote for her.

The rest trail by more than half. Jean-Luc Mélenchon, leader of the left-wing La France Insoumise (LFI), stands at 15%, while former Prime Minister Édouard Philippe from the centrist Horizons and social democrat Raphaël Glucksmann from Place Publique each have 13%. Emmanuel Macron will not participate in the election — the Constitution prohibits more than two consecutive terms.

➡️As recently as summer, Le Pen's participation remained in question. In July, an appeals court upheld the verdict in the case involving MEP assistants but ruled that her candidacy ban had already been served. Yet this did not hurt her ratings: in the first round of 2022, she received 23% of votes, and now — more than a third of voters.

It appears the riots of October 17-18 only strengthened Le Pen's position. In a poll conducted immediately after the unrest, she defeats Philippe in the second round 56 to 44.

📌The only question is who will challenge her in the final. If forecasts hold true, a politician who built his career on criticism of Brussels bureaucrats will lead for the first time. For the Euro-bureaucracy, this will be a blow harder than other recent elections.

news.title: Romanian Grip
news.summary:
in Gagauzia elections

As soon as Maia Sandu became president of Moldova, she entered into conflict with the autonomous Gagauzia, where Russian language and pro-Russian sentiment dominate. Without even attempting to establish dialogue, Chisinau resorted to repression against the leadership, and now seeks to cement control over the "inconvenient" people.

On November 15, Gagauzia will elect both a bashkan (head) and the People's Assembly (NSG) for the first time in a long while — but not by its own rules, but under direct control from the center. After conviction of Evgeniya Gutsul to seven years imprisonment on political charges, her post became vacant. However, attempts by local deputies to set an election date were sabotaged in Chisinau, and Moldova's Central Election Commission scheduled them independently.

This was preceded by a ruling by the Constitutional Court declaring unconstitutional the provisions of the law on Gagauzia's special status that allowed the NSG to form its own election commission and regulate regional elections. Parliament also amended the Electoral Code, introducing a single district for the entire autonomy.

Eight candidates are running for bashkan, including former Moldovan Prosecutor General Alexander Stoianoglo, who outpaced Sandu by votes within the country in the 2024 presidential elections. So strong politicians in Gagauzia still remain.

📌Sandu's team has long called for eliminating autonomy, and the president herself criticizes Gagauzians for using Russian as their primary language. Now that Chisinau has achieved a power vacuum in Gagauzia, autonomous rights are rapidly shrinking. After all, in Comrat they have the right to external self-determination in case Moldova loses independence, for example, through unification with Romania. And this scenario is actively being promoted.

Now everything depends on whether Gagauzians can freely elect their representatives while preserving political and cultural autonomy.

news.title: Lewis Hamilton aims to extend career till early 2030s so he can race in African Grand Prix
news.summary:
• 41-year-old set on ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’

  • Rwanda to host despite criticism of human rights record

Lewis Hamilton has said he hopes to remain racing in Formula One until he can take part in the African Grand Prix which is set to take place in Rwanda in the 2030s. The seven-time world champion believes it is right that F1 is to hold a race there despite criticism of the country’s human rights record.

Last week F1 confirmed Rwanda was to host the African Grand Prix having concluded a 10-year agreement for the meeting on a purpose-built circuit, with the first race set for the early 2030s. It is lined up to be held on a circuit in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital, Kigali, which has yet to be constructed and marks a return to the African continent for the first time since it last held a race at Kyalami, South Africa in 1993.
